cf.title: Add a warning on stats manipulation functions

input.subject: Can we use Statistics Import and Export feature to perforamance testing?

verdict_reasoning: The patch adds one paragraph to an existing docs warning and changes no code. Message #1 shows demand from several PGEcons member companies, and message #2 supports each factor the paragraph names. The only surviving objection, standards-compat-1, is about where the note is placed and is fixable. Wording and the missing rebase are documentation review, outside levels 1-2.

brief.title: Docs warning that restored statistics do not guarantee the same plans
brief.problem: Users want to copy production statistics to a staging server with pg_dump --statistics-only and expect the same plans there. The planner also uses inputs that statistics do not carry, so plans can differ. The patch is meant to stop users from asking this question again.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds one paragraph to the existing warning box on statistics manipulation functions in func-admin.sgml. The paragraph says manually restored statistics do not guarantee the same plans as the source, because relation sizes, index OIDs and configuration parameters affect the planner. There is no code change.
user_visible_surface: New paragraph in the warning on statistics manipulation functions (doc/src/sgml/func/func-admin.sgml).
author_claims: The name "statistics manipulation functions" suggests they can control generated plans, so a warning helps.
Relation sizes, index OIDs and configuration parameters can make plans differ after restoring statistics.
Ryohei Takahashi says the patch prevents user confusion.
brief.thread_state: Ryohei Takahashi approved v1, and Kenichiro Tanaka proposed rewording: "actual relation file sizes", "the creation order of indexes", and adding the actual data range read from indexes. The author has not answered, and a cross-reference patch from vellaipandiyan sm never reached the list.
unclear: The material shows no revised patch after Tanaka's wording suggestions.
CFbot reported the patch needs a rebase in 2026-03, and the thread shows no rebased version.
The patch does not say whether the pg_dump page, which Takahashi asked about, should get the same note.
The proposal does not say whether work_mem effects and other real-data effects, raised by Corey Huinker, belong in the warning.

objections.title: Warning sits on the functions page, not where pg_dump users look
objections.failure_scenario: A user follows the workflow from message #1 and runs pg_dump --statistics-only, then restores the output on staging. They read the pg_dump and pg_restore pages, which do not carry the new warning. They find out only when staging plans differ from production.
objections.argument: The question in message #1 is about pg_dump --statistics-only, and message #3 asked for the note on the pg_dump page. The patch in message #8 changes only func-admin.sgml, which pg_dump users do not need to read, because pg_dump calls pg_restore_relation_stats() for them. No later message settles where the note belongs, so the patch may not stop the repeat question it was written for.
objections.author_must_show: Why does the warning not also belong in, or link from, the pg_dump and pg_restore pages that describe --statistics-only?

critic.reasoning: Message #3 asked for the note on the pg_dump page, and the patch changes only func-admin.sgml. Takahashi accepted v1 in message #9, but no message says why the pg_dump and pg_restore pages need no note or link.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: The warning is about statistics restored from pg_dump --statistics-only output, but the pg_dump and pg_restore pages get no note.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Should the pg_dump and pg_restore pages that describe --statistics-only carry the same note, or a link to it, as message #3 asked?
Do you accept Tanaka's wording from message #13: "actual relation file sizes", "the creation order of indexes", and the actual data range read from indexes?
Should the warning also name work_mem and the other real-data effects that Corey Huinker raised, or say that the list of factors is not complete?
Can you post a rebased version, since CFbot reported in 2026-03 that the patch needs a rebase?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows the statistics import and export documentation would have to pick this up; the visible messages show no committer review of the patch.
committability.liability: One docs paragraph with a short list of factors. The owner signs for its accuracy and for keeping the list in line with planner behaviour.
committability.author_follow_up: The author moved the entry to each new CommitFest through 2026-10, but has not answered the wording suggestions or posted a rebase.

priority.reason: The patch is a 738-byte docs change with demand shown in message #1 and almost no cost after commit. It needs a rebase and a revision that settles the wording and the placement before a committer can take it.

provisional_note: Only the first 3 of 13 messages and the v1 docs hunk were read. The exact wording, the SGML placement after a rebase, and any agreement in later messages could not be checked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Adaptive query optimization: create extented statistics using auto_explain extension
precedents_retrieved.summary: Two patches: one lets the planner use extended (multicolumn) statistics when it estimates join selectivity, and one makes auto_explain create, or only suggest, CREATE STATISTICS for the columns of plan nodes where actual and estimated row counts differ beyond a threshold. The goal is to correct estimates for correlated columns without manual statistics creation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread stalled after the patch stopped building in CI (auto_explain.c used ModifyTableState fields that no longer exist) and review comments were left open. Those comments, from Yugo NAGATA, asked for the reason behind each suggestion and reported redundant suggestions and duplicate ones that fail on pg_statistic_ext_name_index. The CF manager returned it with feedback; no design objection decided it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
As this thread has stalled and the patch hasn't worked in the CI for quite some
time, I'm marking this Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump new feature: exporting functions only
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a pg_dump switch (--functions-only) to dump only stored functions and procedures from a database, without resolving their dependencies on other objects. During the discussion the design moved toward pattern-based include/exclude options per object type (e.g. --routine/--exclude-routine alongside --table, --schema, --extension).
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers asked for a different design: pattern-matching options per object type with matching exclude options, in line with --table and --extension, instead of an all-or-nothing --functions-only switch. The author summarised the new plan and said she would rewrite the patch, but no reworked patch is shown before the deadline. The committer closing the entry concluded that a different design was wanted and that it would not make v15.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Looks clear to me that a different design is wanted here, and that
this won't make it for v15, so I have marked the patch as returned
with feedback in the CF app.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix pg_stat_statements query jumbling to use relation name instead of relation oid
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Geoghegan, Julien Rouhaud, Tom Lane
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes pg_stat_statements query jumbling to hash the relation name instead of the relation OID, so a queryid stays the same after a table is dropped and re-created. The author wanted stable, name-based queryids for use in other extensions such as pgaudit and sql_firewall.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Geoghegan opposed the change, since renaming a table does not make it a different table. Julien Rouhaud and Michael Paquier noted that the patch ignores the schema (and the database), and that renames would change the queryid. Tom Lane said the idea only works if every OID in the jumble (types, operators, functions) is replaced by a name, and that the extra name lookups could cost much performance, so he voted to reject.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
That argument would only hold if *every* use of OIDs in the jumbles
were replaced by names --- not only tables, but types, operators,
functions, etc.  I'm already concerned that the additional name
lookups will cost a lot of performance, and I think adding so many
more would probably be disastrous.

precedents_retrieved.title: proposal of adding 2 new diag items related to parsing the dynamic sql statement
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds two PL/pgSQL GET STACKED DIAGNOSTICS items, later named PG_SQL_TEXT and PG_ERROR_LOCATION, that return the text of a failed dynamic or embedded SQL statement and the error position in it. It extends ErrorData with a query field so EXECUTE errors keep the statement text.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was closed because no new version followed the last review for three weeks. Pavel Stehule's last review left only the documentation wording to fix, and the author waited for other suggestions instead of sending a revision. The author posted a patch on the day of closing, and Zhihong Yu replied with a minor comment.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This update was three weeks ago, and no new version has been
provided, so I am marking this as returned with feedback in the CF
app.

precedents_retrieved.title: multivariate statistics
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds multi-column statistics, defined with `ALTER TABLE ... ADD STATISTICS ON (columns)` and stored in a new catalog `pg_mv_statistic`, so the planner can estimate correlated columns better. Later versions are split into a series: shared infrastructure and functional dependencies, clause reduction, multivariate MCV lists, histograms, and estimation that combines several statistics.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier returned the patch with feedback at the end of the commitfest, citing the review discussion without naming one deciding issue. At that point Heikki Linnakangas found the patches too large to review at once. He also objected that functional dependencies are treated as a boolean property with a threshold, so a small change in the data can change estimates sharply. Kyotaro HORIGUCHI objected that the multivariate logic intrudes too far into clauselist_selectivity and proposed a separate, bottom-up design, and these points were still open.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The problem with a threshold is that around that threshold, even a small change in the data set can drastically change the produced estimates.

precedents_retrieved.title: multivariate statistics
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds user-defined statistics on several columns of one table (alter table ... add statistics on (a, b, c)), stored in a new catalog pg_mv_statistic. ANALYZE builds multivariate MCV lists and histograms, and the planner uses them to estimate clauses on correlated columns instead of assuming independence.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No new version was posted in the last 10 days of the 9.6 commitfest after the entry was marked waiting on author, so Robert Haas returned it with feedback. Open items included missing docs for the new catalog pg_mv_statistic. The author said the patch got too little thorough code review, and the expected reviewers with statistics expertise did not get to it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Since no new version of this patch has been posted in the last 10
days, it seems clear that there will not be time for this to
reasonably become ready for committer and then get committed in the
few hours remaining before the deadline.

precedents_retrieved.title: Implement type input functions for extended statistics types
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds input functions for the extended statistics types pg_ndistinct, pg_dependencies and pg_mcv_list, so that dumped extended statistics can be restored. It parses pg_ndistinct and pg_dependencies with a new yacc grammar and reads pg_mcv_list through byteain().
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry after Tomas Vondra and Tom Lane said dump and reload should start with regular statistics, and that it needs a plan for statistics whose format changes between major versions or whose meaning depends on the environment, such as collation. The patch also had build warnings and failed regression tests, and Andres Freund reported that it crashed in CI. The thread has no author reply after these comments.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
And yes, the main
stumbling block is that you need to have a plan for stats changing
across versions, or even just environmental issues.

precedents_retrieved.title: multivariate statistics
precedents_retrieved.summary: The WIP patch adds `ALTER TABLE ... ADD STATISTICS ON (columns)` and a pg_mv_statistic catalog, so ANALYZE builds statistics on several columns of a table. The planner uses these MCV lists and multi-dimensional histograms to estimate clauses on correlated columns, in place of the independence assumption.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding to review. Michael Paquier moved the patch to the next commitfest after the author said a new version would take more time. A month later he marked it returned with feedback because no new version arrived. The visible messages contain no objection to the design.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
No new version showed up in the last
month and this patch was waiting for input from author.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert recent changes related to handling of 2PC files at recovery
precedents_retrieved.authors: Michael Paquier, Alexander Korotkov, Simon Riggs
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert recent changes related to handling of 2PC files at recovery
Reverted commit(s): Fix handling of orphaned 2PC files in the future at recovery; Fix failures with incorrect epoch handling for 2PC files at recovery; Make use FullTransactionId in 2PC filenames; Speedup 2PC recovery by skipping two phase state files in normal path
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This commit reverts 8f67f994e8ea (down to v13) and c3de0f9eed38 (down to
v17), as these are proving to not be completely correct regarding two
aspects:
- In v17 and newer branches, c3de0f9eed38's check for epoch handling is
incorrect, and does not correctly handle frozen epochs.  A logic closer
to widen_snapshot_xid() should be used.  The 2PC code should try to
integrate deeper with FullTransactionIds, 5a1dfde8334b being not enough.
- In v13 and newer branches, 8f67f994e8ea is a workaround for the real
issue, which is that we should not attempt CLOG lookups without reaching
consistency.  This exists since 728bd991c3c4, and this is reachable with
ProcessTwoPhaseBuffer() called by restoreTwoPhaseData() at the beginning
of recovery.

Per discussion with Noah Misch.

precedents_retrieved.summary:

precedents_retrieved.objection:
Reverts 27838981be9d (some comments are kept).  Per discussion, it does
not seem safe to relax the lock level used for this; in order for it to
be safe, there would have to be memory barriers between the point we set
the flag and the point we set the trasaction Xid, which perhaps would
not be so bad; but there would also have to be barriers at the readers'
side, which from a performance perspective might be bad.

Now maybe this analysis is wrong and it *is* safe for some reason, but
proof of that is not trivial.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Optimize order of GROUP BY keys".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Optimize order of GROUP BY keys".
Reverted commit(s): Optimize order of GROUP BY keys
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit db0d67db2401eb6238ccc04c6407a4fd4f985832 and
several follow-on fixes.  The idea of making a cost-based choice
of the order of the sorting columns is not fundamentally unsound,
but it requires cost information and data statistics that we don't
really have.  For example, relying on procost to distinguish the
relative costs of different sort comparators is pretty pointless
so long as most such comparator functions are labeled with cost 1.0.
Moreover, estimating the number of comparisons done by Quicksort
requires more than just an estimate of the number of distinct values
in the input: you also need some idea of the sizes of the larger
groups, if you want an estimate that's good to better than a factor of
three or so.  That's data that's often unknown or not very reliable.
Worse, to arrive at estimates of the number of calls made to the
lower-order-column comparison functions, the code needs to make
estimates of the numbers of distinct values of multiple columns,
which are necessarily even less trustworthy than per-column stats.
Even if all the inputs are perfectly reliable, the cost algorithm
as-implemented cannot offer useful information about how to order
sorting columns beyond the point at which the average group size
is estimated to drop to 1.

Close inspection of the code added by db0d67db2 shows that there
are also multiple small bugs.  These could have been fixed, but
there's not much point if we don't trust the estimates to be
accurate in-principle.

Finally, the changes in cost_sort's behavior made for very large
changes (often a factor of 2 or so) in the cost estimates for all
sorting operations, not only those for multi-column GROUP BY.
That naturally changes plan choices in many situations, and there's
precious little evidence to show that the changes are for the better.
Given the above doubts about whether the new estimates are really
trustworthy, it's hard to summon much confidence that these changes
are better on the average.

Since we're hard up against the release deadline for v15, let's
revert these changes for now.  We can always try again later.

Note: in v15, I left T_PathKeyInfo in place in nodes.h even though
it's unreferenced.  Removing it would be an ABI break, and it seems
a bit late in the release cycle for that.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P10] adds input functions for extended statistics types and was withdrawn over version and environment portability of stats formats, which does not apply to a docs-only warning. The thread points to no earlier discussion of this warning, so the prior-attempts angle has nothing to raise.

The patch changes no syntax, catalog, GUC or behaviour, so the standards and compatibility angle has little to object to. The only point is where the warning is placed. Wording issues from message #13 are documentation detail and fall outside this angle.

The patch adds one paragraph to func-admin.sgml and changes no code, so it touches no on-disk format, WAL, replication, catalog, wire protocol or extension ABI. This angle has nothing to object to. [P10] is about restoring extended statistics, not about documentation, so it does not apply.
The patch adds one documentation paragraph saying that restored statistics do not guarantee the same plans. It changes no code, privilege, default or exposure, so it raises no security concern.

The patch adds one non-exhaustive paragraph to an existing docs warning. It touches no hot path, no API and no catalog, and adds no dependency, so its maintenance cost is close to zero. The wording points raised in message #13 are documentation review, which is out of scope here. [P10] is about extended statistics input functions and its reason does not apply.

No existing feature or document already gives this warning. The planner docs explain the actual-size scaling (message #6), but they do not say that restored statistics will not reproduce plans. An extension cannot replace a documentation note, and get_relation_info_hook (message #2) only helps users who want to force sizes, so a docs patch remains a reasonable place for the note.

Demand is shown in the material. Message #1 reports that several PGEcons member companies want production statistics on staging servers, and the confusion came up on the list itself. A docs-only paragraph costs almost nothing and adds no burden for non-users. Wording questions in message #13 are for other angles.
